title: Woman breaks 33-year silence over V-shaped UFO sighting above Llangollen hills
excerpt: Alexandra Newby was staying in a caravan at Valle Crucis Abbey when mysterious red lights caught her eye
content:
For more than three decades, Alexandra Newby kept a remarkable secret to herself, fearing she would not be believed if she spoke out about what she saw gliding silently above the North Wales hills in the dead of night.

It was September 1993. The then-21-year-old was staying alone in a caravan, which her family owned, near the shell of the historic Valle Crucis Abbey, near Llangollen.

According to Alexandra, she was looking out towards the ruins of Castell Dinas Brân, when mysterious red lights caught her eye, which she is now convinced was a UFO or UAP (Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena), as it's also known these days.

At first, she feared she was witnessing a plane crash in the making—until she stepped outside into the crisp, silent, morning air and realised that something strange was going on.

‌

Recalling the eerie encounter, in detail for the first time, Alexandra said: "It was in September 1993. It was the early hours of a Wednesday or Thursday morning. I was in the caravan on my own and I had the curtains open.

"As I was sitting there, out the corner of my eye I could see red lights and they were in the area of Dinas Brân about 50ft above it. At first I thought it was a plane coming down and I thought 'Oh my God'."

Alexandra began pulling on her trainers to head outside while keeping her eyes fixed on the sky, quickly realising that something was not right.

"As I was continually watching the lights, I realised it wasn't dropping any altitude and was perfectly maintaining its height. It was going far too slow, if it had been a plane coming down it would have been far faster than that.

‌

"When I got outside, there were a couple of sheep in the field and one of them bleated - and then I realised there was no engine noise, it was completely silent. I was trying to compute what I was seeing, what it could be?"

Alexandra says she was well accustomed to military aircraft passing overhead, as well as local leisure activities.

"We often saw jets flying above, it wasn't a helicopter, there was no noise, we were also familiar with people paragliding in the area," she said.

‌

"I then thought 'Am I seeing a UFO here?' It was the only thing that made any sense. I finished putting my trainers on and went outside the caravan.

"I watched it maintain its height and it very slowly went over the top of Dinas Brân."

Although she could not make out a solid structure in the darkness, she says she clearly saw two sets of lights angling back diagonally from a central light—a formation she later equated to a smaller version of the huge V-shaped craft witnessed by thousands across Arizona and Nevada during the famous Phoenix Lights incident during March 1997.

Among the witnesses to that incident, were the then-Arizona governor Fife Symington and Hollywood star Kurt Russell, and despite official military explanations attempting to account for the sightings, the event remains one of the USA's most famous UAP cases.

‌

However Alexandra's initial curiosity soon turned to fear: "It was moving impossibly slowly, then - I don't know why I did this, probably being young and 21 - I waved at them - trying to let them know we were friendly.

"But as the lights were drawing level with me, I couldn't see any shape, except the lights, I just had this feeling of dread come over me. So I ran back into the caravan and closed the curtains. It was exactly 4.15am."

Alexandra, who is now 54 and lives in Liverpool, never saw the object leave, which she estimated to be size of a jumbo jet across, as she remained in the caravan.

She says she confided what happened in her mum, dad, and boyfriend at the time, but chose not to go public, fearing a sceptical reaction while the still topic remained stigmatised, during the early 1990s.

‌

Today, the subject is discussed far more openly following a landmark 2017 New York Times front-page exposé revealing a secret Pentagon UFO investigation programme, which shifted UAPs from the fringes into mainstream US national security.

Former President Barack Obama has acknowledged on the record that genuine footage exists of aerial objects whose movements cannot be explained.

Congress has subsequently launched landmark public hearings featuring evidence from military aviators and intelligence whistleblowers, prompting the creation of a permanent Pentagon tracking office, while President Donald Trump has ordered a sweeping review and rolling release of declassified government UAP files, as global interest continues to grow.

‌

Having later learned that other locals had also witnessed unexplained lights around Llangollen at the same time Alexandra has finally decided to share her account in light of the more open climate surrounding the phenomenon.

"I have never seen anything like this before and since," Alexandra said: "It was too slow to be anything that we had. I have no doubt that it was something else, I think it was definitely a UFO/UAP."

It appears Alexandra's sighting may have been the same, or similar, to another sighting at Valle Crucis Abbey in 1993, reported by North Wales Live, which also prompted her to come forward, when she discovered the article.

A Colwyn Bay woman known as Karen W and her boyfriend, were reported to have camped overnight at the ruins of Valle Crucis Abbey in Llangollen, in that year, on a dare to spot a reputed "headless monk" ghost.

‌

Instead, a silent, jumbo jet-sized diamond-shaped UFO suddenly appeared 60ft above them, flooding the ruins in bright spotlights and red cross-shaped lights for five terrifying minutes before gliding away toward the mountain.

A former air cadet, Karen said she did not recognise the craft, which was also witnessed by a shocked group collecting firewood nearby, leaving her also seeking answers to the unexplained encounter.
